deliverable_metadata.title: Productive Tensions Catalog — Heidegger and Rhetoric (Gross & Kemmann eds., SUNY 2005)
deliverable_metadata.source: Phase 0 VT1-VT12 seed list (phase0-overview.md §7) augmented by Phase 2 unit tension sections (T1-Tn per unit)
deliverable_metadata.notes: Each tension records dependency_edge (what the conflicting positions share) and conflict_edge (where they diverge); contributors lists ALL units with a stake; synthesis is volume-internal where stated, analyst-flagged with [INTERP] where not.

tensions.title: Centrality vs. Restriction of Rhetoric in Heidegger
tensions.node_a: POSITION:HR-01-GROSS-A-P2 (rhetoric relocated at heart of fundamental ontology)
tensions.node_b: POSITION:HR-07-POGGELER-P1 (rhetoric restricted to Marburg 1923-28; topology of being supplants)

dependency_edge.note: Both contributors cite GA 18 SS 1924 as central evidence; both engage Heidegger's BT §29 (BT 178) reading of Aristotle's Rhetoric

conflict_edge.note: Opposite conclusions about rhetoric's enduring role in Heidegger's thought. Gross tracks FORWARD from 1924 to BT (and to 1959's 'die Sprache spricht'); Pöggeler tracks BACKWARD from 1947 (Aus der Erfahrung des Denkens / topology of being) to Marburg, finding restriction at every junction

tensions.synthesis: The volume's most architectural disagreement: Gross opens with the centrality thesis; Pöggeler closes with the restriction thesis. Hyde, Struever, Kisiel align with Gross on SS 1924 → BT continuity; Gadamer partially affirms (continuity through Befindlichkeit + late-restriction in poetics-only turn); Michalski's philological framing is methodologically sustaining (compatible with Gross's continuity). Gross-B-P10 (HR-01-GROSS-B-T4) reads Pöggeler's restriction-thesis as itself a *symptom* explained by Gross's depoliticization-by-hermeneutics diagnosis — Pöggeler reads late Heidegger and finds rhetoric restricted; Gross reads early Heidegger and explains why late Heidegger looks restricted. The disagreement is generative: each side exposes what the other underplays.

tensions.title: Rhetoric as Dynamis vs. as Technē
tensions.node_a: POSITION:HR-02-GADAMER-P1 + HR-05-STRUEVER-P3 + HR-06-KISIEL-P1 (rhetoric is dynamis, not technē)
tensions.node_b: Implicit: Aristotle's own elsewhere-designation of rhetoric as technē + post-Aristotelian rhetorical-instructional tradition

dependency_edge.note: All three contributors anchor on Aristotle Rhetoric I.2 (1355b25) + Heidegger GA 18 114: 'The technē-designation is incorrect, whereas dynamis is the correct definition'

conflict_edge.note: Dynamis-only reading (defended) vs. technē-tradition (rejected). The Aristotle/Heidegger dispute is internal to Aristotle himself, who designates rhetoric as both — Heidegger's selective reading privileges dynamis as the philosophically constructive register

tensions.synthesis: Three contributors converge on the volume's central Aristotelian-philological commitment. Gadamer's interview is the locus classicus (Ch 2 §II response p. 49). Struever specifies dynamis tou theoresai (Rhet. 1355b26 / GA 18 122) — narrowing Gadamer's broader dynamis-claim to the specific textual anchor. Kisiel: rhetoric is 'first of all not an art but a power, dynamis ... cultivated power of situational insight, phronesis' (p. 146). Gadamer adds a subtle correction (HR-02-GADAMER-T4): 'Heidegger ... began emphatically using the concept of energeia. And so he associated the concept of dynamis with the concept of energeia, and missed the other one' — i.e., the productive-poietic dimension of technē was lost in the dynamis-energeia coupling. The volume's signature Aristotelian commitment is also its most-finely-graded.

tensions.title: Continuity vs. Rupture in Heidegger 1924 → 1927 → post-1933
tensions.node_a: Continuity-readings: HR-01-GROSS, HR-04-HYDE, HR-05-STRUEVER, HR-02-GADAMER (qualified), HR-03-MICHALSKI
tensions.node_b: Rupture/Restriction-readings: HR-07-POGGELER (rhetoric restricted to Marburg; topology of being is the post-1947 succession); HR-06-KISIEL (three-phase model: only Phase 1 is rhetorical)

dependency_edge.note: All contributors agree GA 18 SS 1924 contains a substantive engagement with Aristotle's Rhetoric. All cite BT §§29-30 (Befindlichkeit/Furcht), §§54-60 (call of conscience), §§39-44 (Sorge) as continuous-with or restriction-of the GA 18 framework

conflict_edge.note: Reading direction: forward-from-1924 (centrality, with substantive continuity); backward-from-1947 (restriction, with bounded Marburg episode); three-phase succession (Kisiel: rhetoric → metontology → polemos, only Phase 1 is rhetorical)

tensions.synthesis: The volume contains three reading directions. Forward-readers (Gross, Hyde, Struever) trace 1924 → BT 1927 with substantive continuity; the move 'colonizes' BT from within (Struever) or constitutes its rhetorical genealogy (Gross). Backward-readers (Pöggeler) track 1947 → 1957 → Marburg → final position, finding the topology of being supplants rhetoric. Kisiel's three-phase model (1923-25 Phenomenological-rhetorical / 1933-35 Metontological-Führer / 1935-43 Archaic-Poietic-polemos) is the most articulated middle: rhetoric is restricted to Phase 1 (agreement with Pöggeler) but the *arc* of restriction is itself politically diagnostic (agreement with Gross's depoliticization thesis). Gadamer occupies a 'continuity-with-late-restriction' position — continuous through Befindlichkeit/Mitsein but acknowledges Heidegger's poetics-only turn was 'his weakest area' (Ch 2 p. 56).

tensions.title: Politics — Protopolitical, Tragedy, Silent, or Anti-Political?
tensions.node_a: Protopolitical reading: HR-06-KISIEL-P1 (rhetorical protopolitics, 1923-24 with Arendtian afterlife); HR-05-STRUEVER-P9 (Heideggerian politics of time briefly in SS 1924); HR-01-GROSS-B-P7 (rhetorical pluralism of 1924)
tensions.node_b: Depoliticization → tragedy: HR-01-GROSS-B-P9, P10 (1933 Nazism as political consequence of BT-era depoliticization); HR-04-HYDE-P7 (Heidegger's 1949 'agriculture/extermination' equation correlates with missing rhetoric's ontological status)
tensions.node_c: Silent on / oblique: HR-02-GADAMER-P9 (Heidegger 'erred' politically, proportional acknowledgment); HR-05-STRUEVER-P11 (briefly: 'troubling'); HR-07-POGGELER (Heidegger 'unable to confront' 1933, p. 171, but no extended discussion)

dependency_edge.note: All contributors agree Heidegger's 1933 Nazi commitment is real and philosophically serious; all engage SS 1924 as the alternative-political-philosophical resource that was abandoned

conflict_edge.note: How politics relates to rhetoric in Heidegger: protopolitical-with-Arendtian-recovery (Kisiel/Struever); tragic-consequence-of-depoliticization (Gross/Hyde); oblique-treatment (Gadamer/Pöggeler)

tensions.synthesis: Three contributors with distinct accounts of the rhetoric/politics relation; Kisiel's three-phase table on book p. 149 is the most articulated single position. Gross's diagnosis (Gross-B-P10 supports Gross-B-P9) is causal: the hermeneutic turn that depoliticized rhetoric also predisposed Heidegger to mistake propaganda-pathos for civic-pathos. Kisiel's diagnosis (HR-06-KISIEL-P3) is operational: Heidegger applied Aristotelian phronesis to the propaganda-political situation he himself had diagnosed in 1924. The two diagnoses are mutually reinforcing (per HR-06-KISIEL-T8-cross). Pöggeler's relative silence on the Nazi years is itself a position: the topology of being supplants both rhetoric AND politics.

tensions.title: Pathos as Cognitive Resource vs. Ontological Substrate
tensions.node_a: POSITION:HR-04-HYDE-P1 (pathē as deliberate rhetorical resources for the orator; call of conscience operates 'ontologically as a primordial and emotional form of epideictic rhetoric'; orator's intentional structure preserved)
tensions.node_b: POSITION:HR-01-GROSS-B-P1 (pathos as ontological substrate — 'the very substance in which propositional thought finds its objects and motivation', Intro p. 4; orator dissolved into pre-cognitive Befindlichkeit)

dependency_edge.note: Both contributors cite GA 18 §§ on pathē (esp. 117, 122, 169, 171, 232, 262); both endorse the Aristotle Rhet. II reading of pathē as condition of judgment (krisis); both reject Roman-tradition denigration

conflict_edge.note: Cognitive-rhetorical-resource register (Hyde: orator's intentional structure preserved) vs. ontological-substrate register (Gross: orator dissolved into pre-cognitive disposition). The two readings operate at different registers and are likely not seamlessly compatible

tensions.synthesis: Six contributors stake distinct readings. Gadamer occupies a productive middle (HR-02-GADAMER-T6): pathē are pre-articulate ground (Gross-side) but also bewährt grounds-for-judgment (Hyde-side); the bewährt caveat is the volume's most philosophically careful navigation. Struever reads pathē as 'Befindlichkeiten oriented to others' (GA 18 207, 232) — intrinsically social-interpersonal, supporting Gross. Kisiel's pisteis-equiprimordial-with-aletheia reading (HR-06-KISIEL-P7) is more ontological than Hyde's, building on Gross. Pöggeler's diagnosis (HR-07-POGGELER-P2) is the negative case: Heidegger's gloss pathos = Befindlichkeit IS the moment of restriction — neither cognitive-resource nor ontological-substrate is preserved but rather dissolved into existential attunement.

tensions.title: Hermeneutics Displacing Rhetoric — Gain or Loss?
tensions.node_a: POSITION:HR-01-GROSS-A-P3 (displacement entails 'political and ethical loss'; rhetoric depoliticized in hermeneutic turn; Gadamer 'downplays' the loss)
tensions.node_b: POSITION:HR-02-GADAMER-P7 (Sprachlichkeit / 'rhetoric is the overarching concept for everything that has to do with the other' — hermeneutics IS rhetoric properly understood, conceptually coextensive)

dependency_edge.note: Both contributors cite Dockhorn's 1966 review of Wahrheit und Methode as catalyzing Gadamer's rhetorical second-edition revisions; both engage the Heidegger-Gadamer relation through GA 18 → BT trajectory

conflict_edge.note: Substantive loss-claim (Gross) vs. conceptual-coextension claim (Gadamer). Gross critiques Gadamer's T&M position from outside (Intro III); Gadamer's Ch 2 interview is the response

tensions.synthesis: Per HR-02-GADAMER-T7: Gadamer's position is more nuanced than Gross suggests. At the conceptual level, rhetoric and hermeneutics are coextensive ('It is the same dynamis!', Ch 2 p. 60); at the institutional-pedagogical level, Gadamer admits he never developed a rhetoric pedagogy and that this was a real limitation. Direct intra-volume engagement: Gross's Ch 1 critique is met by Gadamer's Ch 2 interview position. Gross's depoliticization-by-hermeneutics thesis (HR-01-GROSS-B-P10) extends the critique structurally — the 'sweep' of power into discursive backgrounds is a 20th-century outsourcing of rhetorical responsibility to speech-act theory (Searle, Grice, Habermas, Sperber).

tensions.title: Phenomenology vs. Philology — Methodologically
tensions.node_a: POSITION:HR-03-MICHALSKI-P5 (philology is a NECESSARY ELEMENT of hermeneutic phenomenology; Heidegger 'explicitly rejects the title of philosophy in favor of philology even for the region exceeding the horizon of classical philology')
tensions.node_b: Implicit critique from HR-06-KISIEL who treats GA 18 as primarily *political* genesis text, not philological exercise

dependency_edge.note: Both contributors cite GA 18 110 (rhetoric as hermeneutic of Dasein); Michalski's editorial role (Klostermann 2002) gives this framing scholarly weight

conflict_edge.note: Methodological framing: philological-textual operations exceeding into hermeneutic-phenomenological territory (Michalski) vs. rhetorical-political genesis text with Arendtian afterlife (Kisiel)

tensions.synthesis: Michalski (Ch 3) answers the titular question synthetically: phenomenology is hermeneuticized; hermeneutic phenomenology requires the philological moment; and philology in this enlarged sense IS the existentially-ontologically grounded directive of scientific research. Kisiel's protopolitical reading does not contradict this directly but draws different categorial consequences from the same loci. Pöggeler agrees with Michalski's philological framing but restricts the import (HR-07-POGGELER-P3 refines HR-03-MICHALSKI-P1): for Michalski the philological orientation is methodologically sustaining; for Pöggeler it's part of what makes the Marburg engagement a bounded episode.

tensions.title: Alltäglichkeit — Timefulness vs. Ordinariness vs. Restriction-to-Everydayness
tensions.node_a: POSITION:HR-05-STRUEVER-P2 (Alltäglichkeit = timefulness, the catalytic agent of temporality, solvent of eternity); aligned with Gross/Hyde/Kisiel readings of BT 178 as load-bearing positive endorsement
tensions.node_b: POSITION:HR-07-POGGELER-P7 (BT §29 reads Aristotle's Rhetoric as 'first systematic hermeneutic of everydayness' as RESTRICTION — Heidegger confines the political to everydayness/das Man, surrendering the deliberative-public dimension)

dependency_edge.note: All contributors cite BT 178 / GA 18 110 as load-bearing. Struever and Gross use both passages as their epigraphs

conflict_edge.note: Translation contested (timefulness vs. ordinariness, against Blattner) AND interpretive valence contested (load-bearing-endorsement vs. moment-of-confinement)

tensions.synthesis: Hyde takes BT 178 as positive Heidegger acknowledgment (Ch 4 p. 83); Pöggeler reads BT 178 as a momentary acknowledgment soon abandoned (Ch 7 p. 171). Kisiel reads it as constitutive for SS 1924 protopolitics (Ch 6 p. 132). Struever's titular coining ('timefulness') is the volume's most articulated alternative to the Blattner erosion-into-ordinariness thesis. Pöggeler's reading is structurally distinctive: not contesting the translation but reading the same passage as restrictive rather than constitutive — the political dimension is confined to everydayness/das Man, surrendering rhetoric's deliberative-public scope.

tensions.title: GA 18 110 / BT 178 Reception — Load-Bearing Endorsement vs. Architectural Silence
tensions.node_a: Gross, Struever, Hyde, Kisiel, Michalski all foreground GA 18 110 ('Rhetorik ist nichts anderes als die Auslegung des konkreten Daseins, die Hermeneutik des Daseins selbst') as the volume's most-cited single passage; load-bearing positive endorsement of rhetoric's centrality
tensions.node_b: Pöggeler does NOT foreground GA 18 110 (the absence is itself significant per HR-07-POGGELER-T2 and Phase 0 VT9); instead reads BT §29 (which contains substantively similar content) as the moment of restriction

dependency_edge.note: All contributors have access to the passage and its BT §29 partner; all engage Heidegger's reading of Aristotle's Rhetoric

conflict_edge.note: Five contributors use GA 18 110 + BT 178 as positive evidence; Pöggeler's contrastive silence is a rhetorical-argumentative move — the passage does not appear in his counterthesis

tensions.synthesis: The architectural disagreement of VT1 is partially executed at the level of which Heidegger-quotations the contributors foreground. Pöggeler's contrastive omission of the GA 18 110 epigraph is itself a position (Phase 0 §7): the passage that Gross uses as epigraph and Struever uses as titular epigraph is structurally absent from Pöggeler's counterthesis. Pöggeler's implicit position (HR-07-POGGELER-P7): BT §29 + GA 18 110 is the moment Heidegger CONFINES the political to everydayness (das Man), thereby surrendering the deliberative-public dimension Aristotle's Rhetoric had named.

tensions.title: BCAP's Deliberative Emphasis vs. Hyde's Epideictic Emphasis (GA 18 §§13-14)
tensions.node_a: BCAP unit U-FP3a (GA 18 §§13-14): Heidegger's reading centers DELIBERATIVE rhetoric (sumbouleutikon) — practical deliberation (Beratung, krisis) about future action
tensions.node_b: POSITION:HR-04-HYDE-P1 (epideictic emphasis: BT call of conscience is primordial-ontological EPIDEICTIC, not deliberative)

dependency_edge.note: Both readings engage GA 18 §§13-14 + Aristotle Rhet. I.3 (rhetorical-genre typology); both read Heidegger's call of conscience as rhetorically structured

conflict_edge.note: Heidegger himself foregrounds deliberative in GA 18 (per BCAP framing); Hyde imports Aristotle's epideictic genre to capture the conscience phenomenon. Hyde concedes (p. 95) 'Heidegger ... admits' epideictic only briefly (GA 18 125 as 'eine Lobrede')

tensions.synthesis: Hyde's reading EXTENDS Heidegger via Aristotle's typology while remaining textually constrained by Heidegger's actual emphases. Volume tension VT10 is therefore productive: BCAP unit U-FP3a's deliberative reading and Hyde's epideictic reading are both textually grounded but emphasize different Aristotelian genres. Kisiel (HR-06-KISIEL-T10-cross) adds a third rhetorical-genre register: ethos = Entschlossenheit (deliberative-political SZ §60), contrasting with Hyde's ethos = Ruf des Gewissens (epideictic-existential SZ §§54-60). The three readings (deliberative-BCAP, epideictic-Hyde, deliberative-Kisiel) make the BT call-of-conscience block a multi-genre rhetorical event in Phase 4.

tensions.title: BT's Befindlichkeit (BT §§29-30) vs. Gross's Pathos-as-Substrate Genealogy
tensions.node_a: BT pipeline unit BT-D1-U5 records Befindlichkeit (§29) + Furcht (§30) as canonical BT existentialia; these terms are the BT-authoritative renderings
tensions.node_b: POSITION:HR-01-GROSS-B-P1, P8 (pathos does conceptual work BT slightly conceals with the term Befindlichkeit; BT 344 / BT 434 document the substantive narrowing)

dependency_edge.note: Both readings agree on the textual identification (GA 18 122: pathē = Befindlichkeit). Phase 2 unit Michalski-HR-03 also supports the equation in his GA 18 4, 120, 168 references

conflict_edge.note: BT German appendix reads Befindlichkeit as the canonical equivalent (no loss); Gross-B-P8 argues Befindlichkeit is a substantive narrowing of the GA 18 pathos (political-rhetorical content stripped). Pöggeler's HR-07-POGGELER-P2 agrees with Gross on the narrowing but reads it as deliberate restriction

tensions.synthesis: Phase 3D cross-link required: BT pipeline + HR pipeline both treat Befindlichkeit as the institutionalized form of the SS 1924 pathos. The productive cross-pipeline question is whether the institutionalization preserves the substantive content. Gross-B argues no (BT 344 + BT 434 narrow Mitsein into individual resoluteness); Pöggeler agrees but reads as restriction; Michalski's editorial framing is methodologically sustaining (philology-as-hermeneutic-phenomenology preserves the GA 18 register). The cross-pipeline tension is generative for Phase 4 reconciliation.

tensions.title: Kinēsis — Aristotelian Ontology / Protopolitical / Middle-Voice
tensions.node_a: Aristotle pipeline reads kinēsis (Phys. III.1-3, esp. 202b23) as ontologically primary; Met. IX (energeia/dynamis pairing)
tensions.node_b: HR-06-KISIEL reads Heidegger's SS 1924 kinēsis as politically charged (Heidegger's reading of GA 18 §§25-28 with poiētikon-pathētikon as conceptual track for BT poiesis-emphasis); HR-01-GROSS-A reads the same loci through the German middle voice as ontological-stylistic experiment (Intro pp. 20-22, Phys 202b23); HR-05-STRUEVER reads kinesis as the vital motion of life — 'If life, then motion, kinēsis. If motion, then time'

dependency_edge.note: All four readings (Aristotle pipeline + Gross + Struever + Kisiel) engage the same Aristotelian loci (Phys. III.1-3, 202b23, 200b12 archē kinēseōs; Met. IX dynamis/energeia)

conflict_edge.note: Ontologically-primary reading (Aristotle pipeline) vs. politically-charged reading (Kisiel) vs. middle-voice-stylistic reading (Gross) vs. life-temporal reading (Struever). Pöggeler reads close-of-GA 18 kinēsis = poiētikon + pathētikon as the conceptual track for BT poiesis-emphasis (i.e., restriction)

tensions.synthesis: Multi-way reading ripe for Phase 4. Aristotle pipeline's existing PHYS-03 unit needs to be enriched by the three HR readings: Kisiel's protopolitical kinēsis (GA 18 §§25-28 reads political-rhetorically); Gross's middle-voice kinēsis (Phys 202b23 read German-stylistically); Struever's life-temporal kinēsis (the syllogism 'life → motion → time'). Michalski's note 8 catalogs Heidegger's three approaches to kinēsis at Physics III.1-3 (GA 18 287f, 316, 323f) with Themistius/Simplicius commentaries — providing the philological scaffolding. The three readings are mutually enriching, not contradictory; Phase 4 cross-link should preserve the four-way structure (Aristotle / Gross / Struever / Kisiel).
tensions.cross_pipeline_target: Aristotle pipeline PHYS-03 (Physics III); Met. IX (energeia/dynamis)

tension_aggregation_notes.vt1_to_vt12_status: All 12 Phase 0 starting tensions retained (VT1-VT12). VT1 + VT5 are the highest-impact (most contributors, sharpest disagreement). VT10-VT12 are the cross-pipeline tensions flagged for Phase 4. VT6 + VT7 are intra-volume engagement tensions (one contributor critiquing another within the volume).
tension_aggregation_notes.phase2_augmentation: Phase 2 unit T-tensions (HR-01-T1-T8, HR-02-T1-T8, HR-03-T1-T8, HR-04-T1-T9, HR-05-T1-T10, HR-06-T1-T11, HR-07-T1-T7) provided per-unit detail that consolidated cleanly into the 12 volume-level tensions; no new tensions emerged that required adding a VT13.
